authority: Current engineering policy. Current user instructions and observed safety/contracts outrank this registry.

policies.default: Inspect repository/runtime facts before requirements, design, implementation, review, and dependency selection.
exceptions: Trivial self-contained questions with no repository dependency

policies.default: Use each language's native type system, ownership/state, error, concurrency, module, and naming idioms.
exceptions: Real serialization, persistence, protocol, or FFI boundary records named by role

policies.default: Obtain explicit approval for every named new dependency or material feature/tool/service expansion after comparing viable options and exact impact.
exceptions: Already approved exact option within the current task

policies.default: Prefer platform/standard library, then existing approved capability, then a small bounded local implementation, then a lightweight high-performance maintained dependency.
exceptions: Cryptography, civil time, Unicode, complex parsing/protocols, concurrency reclamation, FFI ownership, and similarly deceptive standards work

alternatives: Use a HashDoS-resistant map only at an identified adversarial-key boundary
Use indexmap when insertion order is contractual

policies.default: Use Jiff for timestamps, civil time, IANA zones, DST, and calendar arithmetic; eliminate Chrono from new code.
exceptions: Convert a third-party Chrono value immediately inside an adapter
Use time for justified no_std/protocol/compile-time formatting needs without parallel domain types
policies.review_after: on Jiff major version or project compatibility change

policies.default: Use scc::HashCache for lightweight bounded concurrent in-memory caching.
alternatives: Use Moka only for richer eviction/loading/policy
Use file cache for restart persistence
Use a designed hybrid cache for memory plus disk
Use an external service only for cross-process/shared durability requirements

policies.default: Use pnpm for every new frontend project with one authoritative lockfile.
exceptions: Preserve an existing package manager during unrelated scoped work; migrate only with explicit scope

policies.default: Use stable TanStack Table v9 as the default production table engine.
exceptions: A project constraint or unsupported required behavior proven by comparison

policies.default: Choose exactly one family: TanStack Charts or Mantine Charts plus Recharts 3, based on required chart types and interactions.
alternatives: Use ECharts only when both preferred families fail a demonstrated specialized need
exceptions: A staged migration with an approved removal condition

policies.default: Prefer GPUI with gpui-component; use Slint as the fallback after platform/support comparison.
Apply rust-swift-ffi for Apple boundaries and rust-kotlin-ffi for Android/JVM/KMP boundaries, plus independent FFI review.
exceptions: None without a new architecture decision

policies.default: Choose queue/messaging semantics from actual durability, ordering, fan-out, and operations needs; do not prescribe Kafka or NATS JetStream globally.
Use broadly compatible HTTP/WebSocket/SSE according to semantics; consider WebTransport when compatibility requirements are low and its transport advantages are demonstrated.
Start with an idiomatic portable baseline; require representative profiling/benchmarks, explicit thresholds, safety review, and a portable fallback before advanced optimization.

Never invent primitives or protocols; use maintained audited libraries/platform facilities, safe randomness, secret handling, constant-time behavior where required, and versioned migration/rotation plans.

audit_rules.message: Manifest or lockfile changed without a recorded named dependency approval.
New Chrono usage is forbidden; use Jiff or convert immediately at an adapter boundary.
Tauri, egui, and eframe are excluded; prefer GPUI or an approved Slint exception.
New frontend projects use pnpm; an existing-project package-manager migration needs explicit scope.
Do not introduce TanStack Charts and Mantine Charts/Recharts together.
Name real boundary types by role; avoid Java-style DTO/VO suffixes.
Verify the abstraction represents a real domain capability, ownership boundary, or persistence port.
Record rust-swift-ffi or rust-kotlin-ffi plus FFI review evidence.
